title: Composition of lci space morphisms and the etale case
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $X,Y,W$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the chartwise local complete intersection condition of [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids]: locally on compatible etale scheme charts a map factors as a closed immersion with ideal generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence followed by a smooth morphism. If $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to W$ are local complete intersection morphisms, then $g\circ f:X\to W$ is a local complete intersection morphism. Every etale morphism of algebraic spaces is a local complete intersection morphism. Here etale morphisms are tested on compatible etale scheme charts using [def-weil-etale-morphism]. No flatness of $f$ or $g$, separation, or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 06C8 (lemma-composition-lci); etale clause from Tag 06C9 (lemma-flat-lci), spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 04XX (lemma-etale-smooth) and 06CP (lemma-smooth-syntomic).

proof.text: Let $P$ be the scheme lci condition explicitly defined in [lem-sfb-scheme-lci-etale-locality]. That node verifies the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion], so the existential chart condition of [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids] is equivalent to $P$ on every compatible chart. Indeed, for a space map $v:A\to B$, a chart $U\to A\times_BV$ surjective etale over a surjective etale $V\to B$ makes $U\to A$ surjective etale, which is condition (2) of the criterion. Conversely, assume (1); choose surjective etale scheme atlases $V\to B$ and $U_1\to A$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and put $U\prime=U_1\times_BV$, a scheme because $V\to B$ is representable. Its map to $A\times_BV$ is the base change of $U_1\to A$, so it is surjective etale, and $(U\prime\to U_1\to A,\ V\to B)$ is a presentation diagram, so $U\prime\to V$ has $P$. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $T\to W$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Apply the atlas-existence clause of [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts] first to $g$ and this atlas and then to $f$ and the resulting atlas of $Y$: obtain compatible $U\xrightarrow{a}V\xrightarrow{b}T$, with $U\to X$ and $V\to Y$ surjective etale. The scheme maps $a,b$ have $P$. It suffices to show $ba$ has $P$, since $U\to T$ is then a presentation with surjective source for $gf$.

source.place: Tag 06C8 (lemma-composition-lci), omitted scheme reduction, using preamble to 06C4 and spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03MJ.

proof.text: Fix $u\in U$ and put $v=a(u)$. By $P(b)$ choose an open neighbourhood $V_0\subseteq V$ of $v$ and a factorization $V_0\xrightarrow{i}Q\xrightarrow{p}T$, where $i$ is a closed immersion with locally finite Koszul-regular ideal and $p$ is smooth [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids]. Apply [lem-sfb-lci-polynomial-local-factorization] to $a$, the point $u$, and the target open $V_0$. This gives a neighbourhood $U_0$ of $u$ and a Koszul-regular immersion $i\prime:U_0\to Q\prime=\mathbf A^n_{V_0}$ with $a|_{U_0}$ its projection to $V_0$.

source.place: Tag 069J (lemma-composition-lci), first paragraph and displayed diagram.

proof.text: Set $Q\prime\prime=\mathbf A^n_Q$. The map $j:Q\prime\to Q\prime\prime$ induced by $i$ is a Koszul-regular closed immersion. Here is the polynomial-base-change argument (the special case of Tag 067P needed here). On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Q$ with immersion ideal $I$ generated by a Koszul-regular list $s$, the map is $A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow(A/I)[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, with kernel $IA[t]$. Its Koszul differential for $s$ acts coefficientwise in the monomial basis. A positive-degree cycle has finitely many coefficients, each a cycle in $K_A(s)$; choose a preimage for each coefficient and assemble their finite polynomial sum. Thus every such cycle is a boundary. These affine neighbourhoods cover the immersion, proving the assertion from the definitions.

source.place: Tag 069J, polynomial base change of i; divisors.tex Tag 067P (lemma-flat-base-change-regular-immersion), proved directly for polynomial extension here.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-composition], $ji\prime:U_0\to Q\prime\prime$ is Koszul-regular. The projection $Q\prime\prime\to Q$ is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], hence $Q\prime\prime\to Q\to T$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. By the meaning of Koszul-regular immersion in the composition node, near $u$ the immersion is closed into an open subscheme $O\subseteq Q\prime\prime$ with locally finite Koszul-regular ideal. The map $O\to T$ is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. This is the required local closed-immersion/smooth factorization of $ba$.

source.place: Tag 069J, last paragraph; divisors.tex Tag 067Q (2); morphisms.tex Tag 01VA.

proof.text: The construction works for every $u\in U$, so $P(ba)$ holds. The surjective-source presentation $U\to T$ in step 1 and [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] therefore give $P(gf)$ for algebraic spaces. This also covers $X=\varnothing$, for which the pointwise condition is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 06C8, completion of the scheme reduction.

proof.text: For an etale space map $e:A\to B$, take a compatible scheme presentation with surjective source; its scheme map $h:E\to F$ is etale by [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts]. It is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. Factor $h$ as $E\xrightarrow{1}E\xrightarrow{h}F$. The identity is a closed immersion with zero ideal, generated by the empty list; its Koszul complex has only degree zero [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. This proves $P(h)$, hence the space map is lci by [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] and the locality node used in step 1. No flatness hypothesis on the original $f,g$ entered any step.
